facts.text: Lovelady sprang up in 1872 when the Houston & Great Northern Railroad cut through land owned by pioneer Cyrus Lovelady, after whom the town was named.
The first post office opened on November 8, 1872, marking the town’s official entry into the national postal network.
Within a few years, Lovelady boasted a bustling marketplace complete with livery stables, a blacksmith shop, and several hotels serving travelers and traders.
By 1876 a public school operated out of a local log house, reflecting the community’s early commitment to education.
The town officially incorporated in 1927, formalizing its local government and civic institutions.
Lovelady sits in southern Houston County, where westward tributaries of Tantabogue Creek and eastward tributaries of Gail Creek flow into the Trinity River watershed.
